title: Nobody Has to Fish with You

collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — JUSTICE AND CONSEQUENCES (JUS-01 to JUS-50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Everyday rules, disputes between neighbors, the elders and the council, making things right, losing a role, a night to cool down, wrongful suspicion and evidence that doesn't add up. Consequences are proportionate and never cruel; children get guidance; nobody goes without food, water or shelter; an accusation is not guilt.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

ledger.why: the casting line, carried out as the roles' ages (picks two adults)

collection.description: A villager stopped fishing with someone who told convenient stories, and that person says it is unfair: rule it, or ask more.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (subject) has stopped fishing with (friend). Over the last season, (friend) has told (subject.him/her) one too many convenient stories about who caught what, and where the good spots were. (friend) has gone to the council, saying (subject) is turning people against (friend.him/her), and that it isn't fair.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: The council asks (subject) directly. (subject) admits (subject.he/she) told two friends why. The council asks (subject.him/her) to stop: (subject.his/her) boundaries are (subject.his/her) own, but they shouldn't become everyone's. (subject) agrees. (friend) is told, plainly, that if (friend.he/she) wants (subject)'s trust back, it will take time and straight stories. Some weeks later, (friend) tells a perfectly straight story about a small catch. (subject) notices.

o1__fx.name: Outcome A
o1__fx.text: The council says (subject) may choose whom (subject.he/she) fishes with, and needn't explain it. But (subject) mustn't stop others from fishing with (friend), or spread stories about (friend.him/her). (subject) agrees. (friend) is hurt, and says so, and finds other people to fish with. Whether the two of them ever fish together again is up to them.
